page.title: Mini-CPU Lab — 8-bit Toy ISA
page.heading: Mini-CPU Lab
page.subtitle: 8-bit toy ISA · 4-bit opcode / 4-bit operand · 16 bytes RAM · A/B registers · Carry/Zero flags
guide.heading: Guided beat
isa.lead_html: ISA: NOP LDA a ADD a SUB a STA a LDI n JMP a JC a JZ a OUT HLT — addresses/immediates 0–15, written in decimal (13) or hex (0xD)
isa.note1_html: Operands must be whole numbers 0–15. Anything else (0xZZ, 300, a missing address) stops Assemble with an error naming the line — it is never quietly read as 0. NOP, OUT and HLT ignore an operand when they run, so NOP 7 is a way to put the value 7 in memory.
isa.note2_html: ZERO lights when A ends up 0 after LDI, LDA, ADD or SUB. STA, OUT and jumps leave it alone. Reset clears it, so a JZ before any of those falls through.
isa.note3_html: Registers are 8-bit: 0 − 1 wraps to 255 (and sets CARRY). A countdown from n=0 runs 256 loops, not zero.
isa.note4_html: Program and values share the same 16 words. A STA can overwrite an instruction — even your final HLT, and then the CPU runs on past it.
src.default:
; Guided beat (8 instructions): load 5, store it,
; load 8, add the stored 5, save result, reload, OUT, HLT
LDI 5
STA 14
LDI 8
ADD 14
STA 15
LDA 15
OUT
HLT
guide.intro.body: A canned 8-instruction program is already loaded: load 5, store it at mem[14], load 8, add the stored 5, store the sum at mem[15], reload it, OUT, then HLT. Press Step repeatedly — watch register A and the memory grid light up as PC advances. Edit the source anytime, then Assemble before stepping again.
guide.intro.hint: Tip: amber border on a memory cell marks the current PC. After each Step, this panel narrates fetch / decode / execute.
guide.reset.hint: CPU registers cleared; memory still holds the assembled program. Press Step.
guide.assembleError.hint: Fix the source, then press Assemble.
guide.halted.body: CPU is stopped after HLT. Press Reset to replay the beat, or edit the program and Assemble.
guide.step.hint: Press Step again. Keep watching A and memory.
guide.step.hintDone: Beat complete — Output should be 13 (5+8). Reset to watch again.
guide.run.body: Auto-stepping every 250ms. Watch A, PC, and memory — or press Stop and Step manually for narration.
exec.nop: NOP does nothing. PC already advanced.
exec.lda: LDA {arg}: A ← mem[{arg}] (was {prevA}, now {A}; zero={zero}). Watch A.
exec.add: ADD {arg}: A ← A + mem[{arg}] → {A} (carry={carry}, zero={zero}). Watch A.
exec.sub: SUB {arg}: A ← A − mem[{arg}] → {A} (carry={carry}, zero={zero}). Watch A.
exec.sta: STA {arg}: mem[{arg}] ← A ({A}). Was {prevMem}; watch that memory cell.
exec.ldi: LDI {arg}: A ← immediate {arg} (was {prevA}; zero={zero}). Watch A.
exec.jmp: JMP {arg}: PC ← {arg} (unconditional). Watch PC on the memory grid.
exec.out: OUT: output register ← A ({A}). Watch the Output Register panel.
exec.hlt: HLT: CPU stops. Output = {out}. Press Reset to replay, or edit + Assemble.
log.halted: CPU halted — reset to run again.
asm.badOperand: Line {line}: bad {what} '{arg}' — write a number 0–15 in decimal (13) or hex (0xD)
asm.outOfRangeValue: Line {line}: {what} '{arg}' is out of range — {name} takes 0–15 (the operand is 4 bits)
asm.outOfRangeAddr: Line {line}: address '{arg}' is past the end of memory — addresses are 0–15
